explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates GPT-4o-mini judgments against human ratings from licensed therapists on a subset of 60 dialogues, reporting correlation coefficients for ES-Skills and ES-Value criteria

prompts.notes: Detailed evaluation prompts provided in Appendix tables (references to Table 20, Table 21, Table 26), though exact prompt text not reproduced in the extracted section

guidelines.notes: Detailed definitions provided for ES-Skills criteria (Identification, Comforting, Suggestions, Experience, Informativeness, Consistency, Role-adherence, Expression, Humanness, Overall) and ES-Value perspectives (seeker's and supporter's perspectives)

sample_size.notes: 60 randomly selected dialogues were evaluated by both GPT-4o-mini and expert therapists

quantitative_scores.notes: Minimum correlation value reported across criteria
Maximum correlation value reported across criteria

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4o-mini evaluations showed positive correlations with therapist ratings across all criteria (0.198-0.778), with most correlations being statistically significant, supporting the validity of automated evaluation.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluations assess ES-Skills and ES-Value criteria. Human evaluation also included naturalness assessment for seeker simulator validation.
